summary: Iteration 9 v9 release — backend 25/25 pytest passed against the LIVE preview URL. Frontend landing visual + pricing + library + onboarding-flow + MOCKED scan all verified. ONE CRITICAL BUG FOUND: Landing.jsx submitSignup calls api.post('/auth/register') directly and never stores the returned JWT in localStorage.rl_token, so the subsequent window.location.href='/onboarding' redirect lands on an unauthenticated session and bounces the user to /login — breaking the entire landing-signup → onboarding flow advertised in the spec.

ui_bugs.issue: POST /auth/register response is discarded — the returned token is never persisted to localStorage.rl_token. As a result, redirect to /onboarding fails auth and the user lands on /login. Use the existing useAuth().register() helper from /app/frontend/src/lib/auth.jsx which already does localStorage.setItem('rl_token', data.token) + setUser(data.user). Quick fix: replace `await api.post('/auth/register', payload)` with `await register(payload)` after importing useAuth.

Hard-coded heading 'You've used all 5 AI edits this month' is shown even when a free-tier user (limit=0) hits the modal. Should use the limit from the 402 detail payload or fall back to detail.message.

integration_issues.issue: Bug above breaks this flow end-to-end. /onboarding requires auth, so the user gets redirected to /login. Onboarding wizard itself (step-1 → step-4 → onb-finish → /dashboard) was NOT verifiable through this flow because of the auth break.

Replace the raw api.post('/auth/register', ...) with the existing useAuth().register(payload) helper (it does localStorage.setItem('rl_token', data.token) + setUser). rca_of_the_issue: Landing.jsx::submitSignup hits /auth/register directly via the axios `api` client. The response payload {token, user} is discarded — only `setSignupOk(true)` is called. The redirect `window.location.href='/onboarding'` then issues a fresh page load with no Authorization header (interceptor reads localStorage.rl_token which was never set). The /onboarding route guard sees no user and redirects to /login. Fix: import `useAuth` from `../lib/auth` and call `await register({...})` which handles both token persistence and user state hydration. Two-line code change.
